brief.title: Retake on Inferno
brief.focus: Retake timing and information under a running bomb timer

facts.text: You play the CT side on Inferno.
The bomb is planted at A; 36 s remain on the bomb timer.
One attacker was last seen in A site 14 s ago with an AK-47.
2 of your 2 alive players carry a defuse kit.
Your team has no utility left.
The attackers detonated two molotovs in Pit 16 s ago.
The attackers detonated a smoke in Library 7 s ago.
Your team is positioned: 2 in CT Spawn.
The position of one attacker is unknown.

actions.label: Retake together, clearing Bombsite A first

qualifiers.label: Hold back and go for a late defuse
Send one player ahead to probe while the rest follow
Move as one stack and keep utility for the defuse
Clear the known position with utility first
Save, but take a trade if an attacker is met

evidence.label: Attacker last seen in Bombsite A

followup.heading: A new sighting
followup.stimulus: After about 10 seconds: The attackers detonate a smoke in Balcony.

updates.text: The attackers set off a smoke in Balcony just now.
About 26 seconds now remain on the bomb timer.

responses.label: Pause and take more information first
Adjust the retake to the new information
Fall back and save the weapons

events.action: In the source round, a T player detonated a smoke in Balcony.
events.consequence: It changes what each side can see or hold near there.
events.state: Alive: 2 for your team, 2 for the opposing team. The bomb is planted.

events.consequence: The T side loses a player.
events.state: Alive: 2 for your team, 1 for the opposing team. The bomb is planted.

comparison.roundAction: In the source round, over the next 10 s: 2 players moved from CT Spawn to Arch. Over the next 20 s the team used no utility and got 1 kill and lost no players. Result: T won the round (t win elimination); 0 of the team survived.
comparison.materialInformation: The information that arrived after the decision: The attackers detonate a smoke in Balcony.
comparison.roundFollowup: After the decision the source round continued: A T player detonated a smoke in Balcony. A CT player killed a T player with an M4A1-S (headshot) in Pit. The T side won the round.

debrief.whyItWorks: Arriving as one group keeps every defender within trade distance, so a single attacker cannot win an isolated duel, and it lets utility and the defuse be covered at the same time. Here, 2 players faced 2 with about 36 seconds left.
debrief.cost: It commits the whole team to one line of approach, which is predictable and gives the attackers time to set up crossfires on it.
debrief.assumption: The remaining time is enough to clear the site and finish the defuse, and the known information is not a fake.
debrief.breaksWhen: The timer runs too short for a defuse after the clear, or the attackers hold two angles that the group cannot clear at once.

evidenceReview.explanation: The timer decides how long any plan can take. Here the timer stood near 36 seconds.
A sighting narrows where contact is likely, but its value falls quickly with age. That sighting was about 14 seconds old.
The head count sets how many duels the team can lose and still carry out its plan. Here it was 2 against 2.

debrief.followupReview: The proposed best answer to the new information was: Adjust the retake to the new information. Reasoning: the new information shows where an opponent is or what utility they have used, so adapting the plan is worth more than repeating it.
debrief.strongestAlternative: The closest alternative was to wait for information first, accepting less time on the bomb for a better read on positions.

counterfactual.changedFact: The bomb timer is far shorter than a defuse needs.
counterfactual.effect: No committed retake could finish, and saving the weapons becomes the stronger line.

reveal.principle: On a retake, weigh the seconds a defuse needs against what you actually know: commit while the clock and the numbers support it, and save when they do not.
